title: Arthur Cayley: Collected Mathematical Papers, Source-Checked Modern LaTeX Slice Readers
version: 2026-06-03 Cayley Vol X and Vol V figure repairs
description:
Dedicated Arthur Cayley author record for source-checked modern LaTeX slice readers, repaired diagrams, TeX sources, and continuation manifests. The current reader surface includes a complete source-checked Volume I reader and volume-level slice readers for most collected-papers volumes. This 2026-06-03 refresh adds the scan-backed native TeX reconstruction of the Volume X p. 347 annexed diagram for the 179 irreducible syzygies in Paper 693 and the Volume V p. 463 secondary-caustic plot in Paper 359, replacing reader-visible placeholders in the affected readers and source lanes. It preserves the earlier scan-backed repairs for the Volume IV hexahedron net in Paper 259 and the Volume X theta-characteristic geometric symbols in Paper 701, refreshes the source/manifest supplement, and updates the residual marker scan so the remaining open work is concentrated in dense tables, plates, or table-layout pages. A worker-generated Volume XIII square/conjugate-table patch is preserved as an unverified repair packet but deliberately not promoted because the rotated printed table still needs cell-by-cell audit.

Status at a glance. [########--] public reader coverage: thousands of rendered pages across current volume readers, including rebuilt 421-page Volume II and 485-page Volume XIII readers; [#######---] scan-faithful cleanup: many diagrams, determinant arrays, and known malformed areas repaired, with remaining open work concentrated in dense tables, plates, or table-layout pages tracked in the manifest and residual-marker scan; [#########-] provenance: source TeX chunks, repair packets, audit notes, and GitHub mirror preserved, while large raw provenance remains on the main preservation record.
notes: Dedicated Cayley author DOI. This patch updates selected reader PDFs plus the source/manifest supplement; large raw provenance remains on the main preservation record.
